athenaSetup.createWorkgroup: Create an Athena workgroup and an S3 results location for agents.
athenaSetup.iamUser: Use a dedicated IAM user for agents, with only the permissions agents need, and rotate its keys regularly. Keys from an assumed role expire within hours and Lightdash can't renew them yet, so agents would be refused until you paste new keys.
athenaSetup.attachPolicy: Attach this policy to the IAM user. KMS keys and cross-account catalogs need extra permissions.
athenaSetup.roleInstead: If you rotate keys automatically, you can use an IAM role instead. Attach the permission policy to the role and use this trust policy. The trusted caller also needs permission to assume the role.
athenaSetup.lakeFormationAdmin: Run as a Lake Formation administrator. Use the IAM user ARN, or the role ARN and not the session ARN. Repeat for each permitted table.
athenaSetup.dataFilter: To limit rows or columns, grant a data filter instead. Other grants on the table can still allow more.
athenaSetup.addHelp: Add the access keys, workgroup and results location. Test checks the AWS identity and runs a simple query.

bigquerySetup.grantDataViewer: Grant Data Viewer on each dataset agents may read.
bigquerySetup.bytesDefault: Agent queries use the connection maximum bytes billed. Set an agent limit in the project connection settings.
bigquerySetup.bytesUnlimited: Agent queries have no maximum bytes billed. Change this in the project connection settings.
bigquerySetup.bytesLimited: Agent queries are limited to {{bytes}} bytes billed. Change this in the project connection settings.
bigquerySetup.addHelp: Create a JSON key for the account, upload it here, then select Test.

clickhouseSetup.createUser: Run as a user with CREATE USER permission. Replace the password placeholder. readonly = 2 keeps queries read-only and allows the query settings agents need.
clickhouseSetup.grant: Grant SELECT on the project database, or limit the grant to specific tables. The row policy is a template. Replace the table and condition before you run it. Everyone's agent shares this account's access.
clickhouseSetup.addHelp: Enter the ai_agents user and its password, then select Test and save.

databricksSetup.create: Create a service principal and an OAuth secret in the Databricks account console. Add it to the workspace and give it CAN USE on the SQL warehouse.
databricksSetup.grant: Replace the placeholders and repeat SELECT for each permitted table or view. Unity Catalog row filters and column masks apply to this principal. Grant only the data every agent user may see.
databricksSetup.addHelp: Use the service principal's application ID as the Client ID.

postgresSetup.createRole: Run as a superuser or a role with CREATEROLE. Choose a strong password for this separate login role.
postgresSetup.grant: Grant only the data every agent user may see. Run ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES as each role that creates tables. It applies to new tables from that role.
postgresSetup.rls: Replace the table and condition placeholders. Row-level security does not apply to superusers, roles with BYPASSRLS, or the table owner unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is set.
postgresSetup.columns: To hide sensitive columns, replace table-wide SELECT grants with column grants such as GRANT SELECT (col_a, col_b). A table-wide grant still allows every column.

redshiftSetup.createUser: Run as a superuser or a user with CREATE USER. Use an 8 to 64 character password with uppercase, lowercase and a number. Use ASCII characters. Exclude spaces, quotes, backslashes, slashes and @.
redshiftSetup.grant: Run in the project database. Replace placeholders. Repeat ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for each table owner. It grants access to future tables.
redshiftSetup.policies: These RLS and masking policies are templates. Replace the table, column, type and condition. Match the mask types to the column.
redshiftSetup.warning: Do not give ai_agents superuser, IGNORE RLS or sys:secadmin rights. Check inherited and PUBLIC grants. Everyone shares this account's access. Check policy settings and limits for external and shared tables.

trinoSetup.createTitle: Create or choose the Trino login
trinoSetup.grantTitle: Limit what the login can read
trinoSetup.noCreateUser: Trino has no CREATE USER. Ask an admin to add a user to the password file or LDAP. Turn on password authentication over HTTPS. Without it, Trino does not check the password.
trinoSetup.starburst: On Starburst Galaxy, create a service account with a restricted role. Use its user name and generated password to sign in with basic authentication.
trinoSetup.fileAccess: Set access-control.name=file and point security.config-file to rules.json. Merge these rules above broader rules. Rules match from top to bottom; the first match wins. Use the effective user shown by Test if your authenticator maps the login to another user.
trinoSetup.replacePlaceholders: Replace the user, table and policy placeholders. The filter and columns fields are optional: remove them or supply a row filter and a column mask expression with the right column type. Names in rules are regex literals; escape regex characters in replacements.
trinoSetup.sqlRoles: Use this alternative only with system access control that supports SQL roles and grants. Connector roles, such as Hive roles, need IN "<catalog>" on CREATE ROLE and the role grant. Check inherited and public grants.
trinoSetup.addHelp: Enter the user and password, then select Test. Everyone using agents shares this login's access. Test checks the sign-in, not every grant.
